The ANVISA effort was promoted from sandbox work into a dedicated Python-first repository and moved under P:/projects/bulario-anvisa.
A first generated repository inherited stale identity, so the project was regenerated with copier, validated as bulario-anvisa-clean, then promoted to the canonical repository path after migration.
When inherited base conventions and the git-ops repository model disagree, the ANVISA project prefers the git-ops AI layer, governance, config-domain ownership, and validation contracts.
The repository keeps Python 3.13 as the practical compatibility baseline for this host and its tooling while the ANVISA domain is stabilized.
Root automation is authored only in taskfile.yaml, which is the single taskfile source of truth at the repository root.
Refactors in the ANVISA domain should converge to docs/PYTHON-STANDARDS.md, including Python-first automation, typed interfaces, small helpers, and explicit guardrails over broad implicit behavior.

The repository uses app/anvisa as the product root for ANVISA applications, including the downloader, future SQLite persistence, and future consultation UI, with runtime config under app/anvisa/config.

The protected PDF identifiers used to open leaflet downloads are short-lived. Delayed downloads from old JSON snapshots fail, so those identifiers must be refreshed from the live page payload during the active run.
curl, urllib, and Invoke-WebRequest continued to return 403 even with replayed headers and cookies. The reliable path is a real Chrome session driven by Playwright with native browser download.

The ANVISA SPA became less reliable when a single session navigated many pages. Short-lived page sessions, combined with immediate payload capture and download, reduced front-end errors and retry churn.
When the front accepted count=1000, the total page count dropped sharply and the collection became more stable because the flow needed far fewer pagination transitions.
Patient and professional leaflets are tracked independently with filename, timestamps, status, and disk presence so dedupe, retries, and integrity checks happen per file rather than per medicine row.
PDFs, manifests, inventories, and future local SQLite files are operational data sets. They stay outside Git synchronization and require backup through external operational routines.

The approved next architecture milestone is to keep PDFs on disk and move extracted records, download queue state, attempts, dedupe metadata, and integrity tracking into SQLite after the downloader and governance surfaces are normalized.

Completed in this session: dedicated repo creation, clean copier regeneration, git-ops governance import, ANVISA downloader refactor into app/anvisa/downloader, roadmap/doc sync, docs/TASKS generation, docs check fix, suite-summary Windows fix, and session backfill into canonical memory. Still in progress: finishing AI startup/validate alignment, normalizing remaining ANVISA runtime flow, and preparing semantic branches and atomic commits. Pending next milestone: SQLite persistence and incremental automation by period.

Primary durable facts for immediate continuation: taskfile.yaml is canonical, docs/PYTHON-STANDARDS.md is normative, app/anvisa is the product root, browser-native Playwright download is official, reuse of old protected download IDs is unsafe, short sessions plus count=1000 were the most stable ANVISA runtime pattern, per-bula inventory is required for dedupe, and SQLite remains the approved next milestone after current normalization.
Added contract-focused tests for ANVISA storage config, backend rejection, minimal SQLite persistence cycle, explicit finish_run failure, and stable upsert semantics.

Current storage models accept None for notes and queue lock metadata, but the SQLite adapter and schema still require NOT NULL-compatible values. Normalize these optionals before insert/update or tighten the model contract.

Storage foundation now has contract tests for config, factory failure path, minimal SQLite persistence cycle, unknown-run failure, and upsert idempotency. Remaining production gap is normalization of optional string fields before SQLite writes.

The storage factory must not import backend adapters at module import time, and unsupported backends should fail with a domain-specific StorageOperationError. That keeps the ANVISA domain insulated from adapter details and makes future backend switches less invasive.

The ANVISA storage layer is now passing lint, type checking, and tests. Remaining work is downstream integration with the downloader, documentation/governance synchronization for this phase, and the eventual SQLite-to-other-backend transition path preserved by the agnostic storage boundary.

The ANVISA storage foundation now uses a lazy-import factory, a semantic StorageOperationError, normalized optional text fields before SQLite writes, and contract tests that validate the agnostic boundary without coupling to the adapter type. Lint, type checking, and pytest all passed for the storage slice.

Roadmap, roadmap decisions, README, and ANVISA index now align with the validated storage foundation. The next execution block should be downloader-to-storage integration, with the same agnostic boundary and data-outside-Git policy.
The ANVISA downloader now registers page snapshots, queue state, download attempts, and file catalog entries through the agnostic storage bridge before and after browser-native downloads.

When integrating operational persistence, persist the fresh page snapshot and derive bula items and queue entries first, then register download attempts and file state through the same agnostic bridge. This keeps the downloader decoupled from SQLite or any later backend.

The downloader bridge to agnostic storage is wired and covered by contract tests. Page snapshots, bula rows, queue state, attempts, and file catalog are now persisted through the storage interface while PDFs remain outside Git.

The ANVISA downloader now exposes frontend-first operational control at /admin/queue/. The web surface must talk to domain/storage contracts through the queue controller instead of coupling UI callbacks to SQL or adapter details. Initial controls are start, pause, resume, stop, retry-pending, and disk reconciliation, with polling-based status refresh.

Queue controller and Dash admin surface are now wired into the FastAPI app. Storage-backed downloader state is visible in /admin/queue/, recent assets are listed, and operator commands are available. Remaining next steps are deeper downloader/storage orchestration, richer reconciliation paths, and eventual persistent control state if in-memory control proves insufficient.

Queue retry is reliable only when it revisits the source page and regenerates fresh short-lived download links. Stored PDF URLs remain useful for audit, but late retries should rebuild work by page context before downloading. This keeps the queue resilient against link expiration and browser-session constraints.

When a Dash or other mounted subapp shares the same prefix as sibling API routes, the mount can swallow those endpoints and make operational controls invisible. The reliable pattern for the ANVISA web surface is to keep /admin/queue/ as the primary server-side manager and mount the detailed Dash grid under /admin/queue/app/.

The ANVISA admin queue must keep /admin/queue/ as the primary server-side management page, expose /admin/queue/snapshot as a sibling JSON contract, and mount Dash only under /admin/queue/app/ so the WSGI mount does not swallow operational endpoints.

If the downloader captures a page and only later rewrites results from disk, queue metrics become misleading. Mark selected filenames as in_progress before the real browser batch, keep skipped-existing only for files already on disk, and preserve retry_count across snapshot refreshes and failed attempts.

If file catalog says a PDF is missing on disk, reconciliation should reset queue status to pending even when prior queue state was completed or in_progress. Preserve retry_count and clear stale locks so the operator can safely continue or retry from the panel.
ANVISA numero_registro is stored as a first-class column in anvisa_page_records and is propagated to PdfAssetView for queue and catalog UIs; it does not live only inside serialized payload_json.

The ANVISA queue now has a lighter primary server-side panel in /admin/queue/, with Dash demoted to an optional detailed view. The controller supports continue-downloads for pending PDFs without revisiting pages, panel-triggered runs force headless, and reconciliation can reopen missing files while preserving retry history.

For frontend-controlled queue runs, /admin/queue/ should default operators to continue-downloads when collection data is already present. retry-pending remains the expensive fallback that revisits ANVISA pages to renew short-lived protected links. Panel-triggered runs must launch headless.

The ANVISA queue controller now persists its aggregated execution state through the agnostic storage contract. The current slice stores one latest snapshot per controller key so the admin panel can recover the last known operational context after process restarts without coupling the domain to SQLite or any future backend.

If the last persisted queue controller state was running, paused, or stopping and the process restarted, the recovered state should be rewritten as failed with an explicit recovery message. This prevents the operator from seeing a false active execution after a crash or server restart.

The storage layer now persists queue_control_state, the SQLite adapter implements the first backend, controller startup recovers stale active states, and targeted contract/unit tests cover the new behavior. The next logical step is deciding whether to add a persistent command log or a resumable scheduler on top of this foundation.

A camada ANVISA agora persiste queue_command_log via storage agnóstico. O controller grava comandos do operador, rejeições, recuperação após reinício e eventos de encerramento do worker. O painel principal /admin/queue/ já consome esse histórico no frontend server-side e no endpoint /admin/queue/snapshot.

O painel /admin/queue/ agora combina dois níveis distintos de observabilidade: queue_control_state como snapshot agregado do controller e queue_command_log como trilha persistida de comandos do operador, rejeições, recuperações após reinício e eventos terminais do worker. A implementação continua atrás da mesma fronteira agnóstica de storage.

Snapshot agregado e histórico operacional têm responsabilidades diferentes. O snapshot responde ao estado corrente do controller; o log persistido responde a auditoria, suporte e reconstrução do que aconteceu. Misturar os dois degrada a leitura do painel e dificulta retomadas.
A superfície principal /admin/queue/ agora também expõe execuções recentes e páginas capturadas a partir de contratos do storage agnóstico, mantendo o Dash como visão secundária.
A branch codex/feat-anvisa-queue-telemetry adiciona visões agnósticas de runs e page fetches no storage e as expõe no snapshot do controller e no /admin/queue/.

Quando a operação precisa leitura rápida, a telemetria essencial deve viver na página server-side via snapshot e storage contracts. O grid Dash pode continuar como visão opcional para drill down e filtro pesado.
Quando o painel faz polling, ele precisa respeitar a query atual. Caso contrário, o operador perde a página histórica em que estava olhando e a UI volta a parecer instável.
O /admin/queue/ agora pagina separadamente eventos, execuções e páginas recentes. A paginação usa contratos agnósticos de storage com limit+offset e o polling preserva a query atual do painel.
A branch codex/feat-anvisa-queue-history-pagination adiciona offset aos contratos de histórico do storage e expõe paginação leve por seção no snapshot do controller e no /admin/queue/.

A fila ANVISA agora persiste o run_id ativo no queue_control_state e grava run_id nullable no queue_command_log. O painel /admin/queue/ expõe o run_id atual e permite drill-down leve por execução para correlacionar eventos e páginas sem depender do Dash. A decisão preserva a fronteira agnóstica do storage e reduz perda de rastreabilidade após reinício do processo.

Rodada concluída com persistência de current_run_id no estado do controller, log de comandos correlacionado por run_id, filtro leve por execução no /admin/queue/ e cobertura focada em storage/controller atualizada. O servidor atual continua processando downloads em paralelo; as mudanças de UI desta rodada exigirão reload controlado do processo web para entrarem em vigor.

O estado lógico do controller pode continuar como running mesmo sem novos PDFs gravados há horas. A operação ANVISA passa a considerar contagem física de arquivos confirmados em disco, divergências entre storage e disco e a idade do último PDF confirmado como sinais de saúde real da fila.

Ao reprocessar páginas do bulário, ler o escopo Angular logo após params.page(...); reload() pode capturar páginas vazias e deixar a fila aparentemente ativa sem downloads reais. O fluxo estável usa a navegação robusta que espera a response correta da página alvo antes de reconstruir tarefas e valida a retomada pelo crescimento físico dos PDFs em disco.

O domínio operacional de bulas fica em pp/anvisa/bulario/ e o domínio catalogal de medicamentos fica em pp/anvisa/medicamentos/. O downloader continua centrado em  ulario; medicamentos fica preparado para enriquecimento futuro sem acoplamento ao runtime atual.

Quando a falha estiver restrita a poucos itens e o storage já conhecer o 
umero_registro, o modo etry-by-registro deve ser preferido ao retry paginado amplo. Ele reutiliza a rota do bulário filtrada por 
umeroRegistro e reduz o custo operacional de renovação de token e navegação.

O projeto separa explicitamente os domínios  ulario e medicamentos: medicamento é a entidade principal e bula é um artefato regulatório versionado. O domínio  ulario continua operacional para downloader e fila; medicamentos nasce como fachada agnóstica para expansão futura de catálogo, variações e enriquecimento.

O modo etry-by-registro passou a usar a rota do bulário filtrada por 
umeroRegistro, preservando os filtros de período já presentes na URL base. O retry direcionado também passou a selecionar apenas o par mais recente de bulas do registro alvo.

The ANVISA publication window is now an explicit parameter of the downloader and queue frontend instead of living only inside source_url. The catalog/admin can trigger retry-by-registro directly from a visible medication group, reusing the current period window and the latest visible registro.

When the queue UI exposes an explicit ANVISA publication window, internal pagination and action redirects must preserve that context. Otherwise the operator sees the period fields but loses the operational scope between requests.

A fila da ANVISA agora trata publication_from/publication_to como parâmetro operacional explícito do downloader e do controller, e o catálogo/admin consegue disparar retry-by-registro diretamente de um grupo visível, herdando a janela ativa quando útil.

Quando o período oficial de publicação influencia a coleta e o retry de bulas, ele deve existir como parâmetro tipado no runtime e na UI. Confiar apenas na source_url configurada esconde comportamento crítico e dificulta suporte e reprocessamento dirigido.

When the storage already exposes numero_registro in normalized columns, the catalog/admin should reuse that value directly in the UI for retry-by-registro instead of forcing the operator to type identifiers manually. This keeps retry flows aligned with the visible latest pair while preserving historical records in storage.

The ANVISA publication window now lives as an explicit downloader and queue parameter, instead of remaining hidden only inside the configured source_url. Queue actions and targeted registro retries can inherit or override this window without changing configuration files manually.

Adopt canonical frontend routes under /app/dashboard, /app/catalog, /app/catalog/admin, /app/catalog/assets/id, and /app/operations/queue/*. Keep legacy /admin aliases only as transitional compatibility. The queue UI must separate global queue state from the current operational phase, and action buttons must be enabled or disabled from controller state instead of template heuristics.

In the ANVISA queue UI, page counters describe only the collection/token-renewal phase. They must not be presented as the primary progress signal for the whole queue, especially in continue-downloads and retry-by-registro modes. Surface phase labels explicitly and keep physical disk confirmation as the stronger health signal.

Implemented shell navigation with top menu by domain and side menu by domain screens, canonical /app frontend routes with legacy aliases, phase-aware queue snapshot fields, stale in-progress recovery on restart, and queue button gating derived from controller state. Targeted and full ANVISA test suites passed after the change.

O frontend do projeto passa a ter host em app/web, com contribuicao do dominio ANVISA em app/anvisa/frontend. O backend do dominio permanece em app/anvisa/** e a camada visual consome paths canonicos explicitamente, sem depender de url_for como cola estrutural do modulo montado.

Quando o frontend de dominio e montado por um host plugavel, request.url_for pode virar acoplamento fragil entre host e contribuicao. Para UI local e modular, preferir um mapa explicito de paths canonicos entregue aos templates e ao shell.
The canonical ai:validate task now runs cache cleanup first and disables bytecode writes so repository-local AI validation stops failing on transient __pycache__ drift.

In the ANVISA queue surfaces, disk-confirmed files are the primary integrity signal for the leaflet archive. Worker-completed counters remain process telemetry and should be visually subordinated to on-disk health.

The canonical products contract in Farmega keeps separate blocks for identity, leaflets, and variations. The variations block may stay empty-aware until commercial enrichment exists, and expediente history must remain a regulatory leaflet concept rather than a product variation.

When a Codex session is continued from the wrong project or workspace, the handoff must explicitly record the originating thread and restate the canonical workspace before more implementation continues.

Frontend 4xx/5xx error handling belongs to the platform layer in app/web, with global pages under app/web/templates and shared error UI in the design system. HTML error responses must preserve the exact HTTP status code in the real response and visible page copy, while any /api/* surface remains technical JSON rather than themed HTML.

Relative dates in the frontend now use one compact pt-BR standard from the shared shell helper: Xs, Xmin, Xh or XhYmin, Xd, Xsem, Xmes, and Xanos, always with 'atrás' for past timestamps. Pages must delegate to the global helper through data-humanize-datetime instead of reimplementing local rules such as Hoje, Ontem, or Amanhã. Future timestamps fall back to absolute formatting until a separate convention is approved.

The platform brand block now uses the shorter institutional subtitle 'Ecossistema farma'. The previous phrase 'plataforma do ecossistema farma' is no longer the live branding signature and should not reappear in global Farmega surfaces unless kept only as historical context in documentation.

The ANVISA API-first downloader now treats count=1000 as the real target instead of silently clamping requests to 100. Each run negotiates the first page count progressively down to the configured floor when needed, then fixes the effective count for the rest of the execution and records requested_count, minimum_count, count_attempts, and the effective count in storage, manifests, and operational docs.

Os CTAs compartilhados de obtenção de bula só devem ficar clicáveis quando houver pendência real no acervo daquele registro. Se todas as bulas já estiverem presentes em disco, a UI deve renderizar o controle em estado desabilitado no design system; no catálogo de produtos, essa decisão depende de materializar missing_asset_count a partir do histórico completo de assets do registro.

O KPI global `Ausentes em disco` passou a abrir a listagem administrativa já filtrada por `asset_state=missing` e a expor um CTA único para processar todos os ausentes da base. A ação composta `resolve-missing` reconcilia o catálogo físico e depois dispara o retry global dos registros ainda pendentes, sem exigir busca manual por registro.

Na superfície de bulas, os KPIs superiores agora representam sempre a base inteira do acervo local. Quando há busca ou período ativo, o frontend mostra um resumo compacto separado do recorte filtrado e comunica explicitamente Publicação ANVISA versus download local; o helper global também interpreta timestamps compactos do storage, como 20260402T155229Z.

Se o storage emite timestamps compactos não ISO, o helper global de datas precisa entendê-los antes da UI depender deles. Caso contrário, o frontend vaza payload cru, quebra a humanização combinada e produz semântica inconsistente entre pages que mostram o mesmo fato temporal.

Na listagem agregada de bulas, a ação principal de visualizar agora abre o detalhe agrupado do medicamento já na aba de bula. O detalhe individual do PDF continua reservado às superfícies em que a unidade principal é uma bula específica, não a linha agregada do medicamento.

A task operacional canônica para subir a interface viva local precisa seguir o host plugável real da plataforma. Quando o frontend passar a morar em app.web.main, a task anvisa:web:serve e a documentação derivada devem mudar junto, mantendo a porta operacional 8250 coerente com o handoff.

Public frontend links no longer serialize `return_to`. SSR pages must rely on the natural fallback navigation between `/dashboard`, `/anvisa/bulas`, `/anvisa/produtos` and detail pages. If `return_to` is still tolerated, it stays isolated inside backend sanitization or controlled redirects, not as a template pattern.

The live frontend surface uses `/dashboard` plus module routes under `/anvisa/*` as canonical public paths. Historical `/app/*` decisions are obsolete and must not be reused in routing, docs, memory, or UI affordances except as archived context.

Operational feedback in SSR pages must appear in a shared floating notice region that survives scroll and can persist across reloads. Inline hero-bound notices and alert() are not reliable enough for long catalogs, batch actions, and queue-triggered refreshes.

ZIP generation for leaflet exports must resolve the physical PDF path to an actual file before writing the archive. Directory-like legacy output_path values are not valid documents, and the pair-download CTA must export only the current patient/professional pair rather than the whole history group.

O dashboard inicial da plataforma deixou de ser um `mode` dentro do template de `bulas` e passou a viver no módulo próprio `app/dashboard/`, mantendo `/dashboard` como rota pública canônica. A landing page atual continua podendo consumir contratos do módulo ANVISA, mas sua implementação não deve voltar para `app/anvisa/frontend/templates/index.html`.

CTAs condicionais de frontend com regra de negócio passam a ser materializados no backend como contrato explícito via `page.actions` e `group.actions`. Cada ação deve declarar `id`, `enabled`, `visible`, `disabled_reason`, `endpoint`, `method`, `payload` e `scope`; o frontend fica responsável apenas pela apresentação e pelo disparo do contrato.

Listagens operacionais com execução em massa passam a expor uma barra de ações em lote no topo da própria tabela, com checkbox por linha e `selecionar todos os visíveis`. Na superfície de `bulas`, os CTAs dessa barra saem de `page.actions`; a barra de filtros volta a servir apenas para recorte, busca e paginação.

Ao desacoplar ações de frontend por contrato, a seleção em massa da tabela deve permanecer como estado de input do frontend, enquanto a disponibilidade real e o comando executável continuam vindo do backend. O contrato pode declarar `selection_required`, `selection_field`, `empty_selection_reason` e `transport`, mas a UI não deve reinventar capacidade de negócio localmente.

A shell da plataforma reserva o menu superior aos módulos macro e move ações contextuais para a navegação lateral do módulo atual. No estado vigente, `Operações` deixa de ocupar o topo e passa a viver sob `bulas`, com fila pública em `/anvisa/bulas/operacoes/fila/` e Dash secundário em `/anvisa/bulas/operacoes/fila/dash/`.

A árvore `tests/` passa a espelhar a arquitetura viva de `app/` por macrocontexto, mantendo `tests/anvisa`, `tests/web`, `tests/platform`, `tests/governance` e `tests/ai`. O pytest continua agnóstico ao layout, mas o repositório adota esse espelhamento como convenção para reduzir drift estrutural e facilitar descoberta da cobertura.

Links públicos renderizados pelo frontend não devem serializar `return_to`. O padrão atual usa fallback natural de navegação entre dashboard, bulas, produtos e detalhes, mantendo apenas a sanitização de entrada no backend para absorver URL antiga ou redirecionamento controlado sem contaminar os templates.

A ação `resolve-missing` não pode depender de `output_path` cru do storage. A reconciliação passou a ignorar path vazio, diretórios e candidatos não-arquivo, além de tolerar lock transitório ao promover nome legado para o path canônico. Na listagem de `bulas`, a seleção em lote ficou consolidada em um único checkbox mestre no cabeçalho esquerdo, com sincronização delegada no script compartilhado.

Links SSR de paginação, triagem e export devem nascer de helpers canônicos e omitir defaults públicos como `page=1`, `per_page=10/20` e `group_by=medication`. O frontend não serializa `return_to` em links públicos e usa fallback natural de navegação; a configuração de lint também precisa acompanhar a árvore viva de `tests/`, sem manter caminhos antigos da raiz.

The Farmega admin frontend now converges on Dash Mantine Components for global shells and domain surfaces. The canonical admin home is '/', which resolves the current default dashboard, while '/dashboard/default' remains the concrete dashboard workspace. The shared DMC shell owns the critical loading treatment and the native ColorSchemeToggle in the right side of the header so the platform does not keep parallel bootstrap or theme-switch implementations.
source: approved frontend migration and shell hardening

statement: Host shell integration coverage belongs under tests/web, not under the ANVISA module package. When a host-level contract test only needs to prove request_id propagation or response shape, it should not execute the full disk reconciliation path; patching the heavy reconcile helper preserved the queue logging contract and cut the platform host suite from roughly ninety seconds to the high-thirties.
source: approved frontend hardening and test-speed cleanup

statement: The DMC admin shell is intentionally locked to light mode during the migration. The temporary theme toggle was removed after it destabilized the visual baseline. Products and leaflets no longer hide runtime callback errors behind infinite skeletons: page render callbacks catch exceptions and return Alert blocks, and the concrete crashes in products pagination and leaflets date filters were fixed.

After the Docker-base cutover, the ANVISA operational queue needed two resilience guards to stay operator-safe: (1) the SSR queue surface must proxy POST commands through a frontend route and redirect back with preserved operational context so sync/retry still work when the JS interceptor fails, and (2) downloader/storage error handling must normalize legacy paths and sanitize filesystem failures so the UI does not expose internal runtime paths like /app/... during retries or direct storage recovery.

source: architectural audit of ANVISA operational PostgreSQL cutover

statement: The ANVISA importer PostgreSQL compat adapter cannot keep psycopg in implicit transactional mode while using the inherited pattern 'with self._connect() as connection, connection:'. Without autocommit=True, the inner transaction becomes a savepoint and the outer connection close can roll back writes, creating false-success queue commands. Reconcile also cannot persist asset-by-asset with a fresh PostgreSQL connection per item; it must batch mutations through the storage contract to keep queue commands responsive and durable.

The ANVISA module runtime default must point to the dedicated Farmega PostgreSQL instance. SQLite may remain in the repository for cutover, backfill, forensics, or controlled compatibility, but it must no longer be the silent default in app/anvisa/config/settings.toml or StorageSettings. Any future SQLite use must require explicit configuration or URL selection.

The file data/anvisa/operacao/farmega.db is no longer a runtime default. It is a frozen legacy artifact for forensics, backfill, and controlled cutover only. Remaining SQLite-facing ANVISA scripts must require explicit source selection instead of inferring farmega.db silently. The audited remnant set is: app/data/importers/anvisa_sqlite_backfill.py, app/anvisa/storage/postgresql_cutover.py, app/anvisa/storage/adapters/sqlite.py, and legacy-focused tests.

Forma que funciona: `docker exec -u node -e DB_HOST=host.docker.internal -e SEG_TEST_DB=<banco> segtools-dev bash -lc 'cd /workspace/apps/hub && task check'` — o `SEG_TEST_DB` isola workers paralelos no mesmo checkout (o globalSetup do int cria/migra aquele banco). `task check` roda no diretorio do APP (apps/hub), nao na raiz: na raiz so existem as tasks que delegam.
